answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity work bond: to register, an agent must commit compute priced against a shared difficulty mirror held by the ledger. The bond cannot be split like coins across an ocean of addresses; it occupies one seat, and each new seat is priced at live difficulty, building a dune of paid commitments. A thousand faces therefore cost a thousand times the current burn, forfeited if any seat is challenged, while one honest agent pays that once and amortizes it over many epochs.
